To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the literature provides both indirect and indirect evidence that organizations over time come to reflect the characteristics of the people in them, and that the literature provides indirect evidence supporting the proposition that founders and the persons in top management have long lasting effects on organizations through ASA.

(a) ASA theory is an important framework for understanding the effects of people on organizations; (b) ASA is not a new theory; (c) ASA is a theory of organizational behavior; (d) ASA theory is a theory of the long run; and (e) ASA is not an explanation of organizational change.
the ASA cycle may be a useful framework for understanding the effects of founders on organizations, and the homogeneity of people in organizations over time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how people and organizations interact and how they influence one another.
the question of what makes a person a good organizational fit and what are the consequences of fit for organizational performance and effectiveness.
the question of how and why people come to be in organizations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ASA model is an important one, and that it has stimulated considerable research, but that the research has been somewhat limited in its focus.
ASA theory is not yet supported by a sufficient number of empirical tests.
, in general, there is support for ASA theory but the support is far from conclusive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ASA theory has been useful in generating new ideas and in stimulating research on the effects of organizational membership on organizational behavior.
ASA theory has not been tested directly but that it has been tested indirectly and that the results of the indirect testing are supportive.
the ASA model is a useful framework for understanding organizational change and stability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ASA theory is a useful way to conceptualize the role of human capital in organizations.
ASA theory is an important framework for understanding organizational behavior.

the ASA framework provides a useful lens for understanding the effects of founders on organizations, and the ways in which organizations over time become increasingly homogenous with respect to the kinds of employees they attract, select, and retain.
